A.explanation: This uses only the change in speed $20 - 15 = 5$ $\text{m s}^{-1}$, ignoring that velocity reverses direction on rebound.

B.explanation: This uses only the rebound momentum $0.16 \times 15$ divided by time, ignoring the initial momentum before impact.

C.explanation: This uses only the initial momentum $0.16 \times 20$ divided by time, ignoring the rebound momentum in the opposite direction.

D.explanation: The total change of momentum is $0.16 \times (20+15)$ divided by $1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{s}$, giving $5600$ $\text{N}$.

hints: Notice the ball reverses direction, so take one direction as positive and give the incoming $20$ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and rebound $15$ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ opposite signs.
Recall impulse equals change in momentum, $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m(v-u)$, so the $20$ and $15$ add when finding the magnitude of $\Delta p$.
Convert the contact time $1.0$ $\text{ms}$ to $1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{s}$, then divide the $5.6$ $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ change in momentum by this time.
walkthrough: Choose a positive direction, for example away from the wall. Then initial velocity $u = -20$ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and final velocity $v = +15$ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ for the $0.16$ $\text{kg}$ ball.
Use change in momentum $\Delta p = mv - mu = m(v-u)$. Reversal means subtract a negative value.
Use average force from impulse $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$ with $\Delta t = 1.0$ $\text{ms} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{s}$.
Calculate $F = 5.6 / (1.0 \times 10^{-3}) = 5600$ $\text{N}$ away from the wall. This is option D.
